title: TissueCyte Specimen Embedding Acrylamide Coembedding
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf65jrg6
materials: Thermal gloves for handling hot glass beaker
NOTE: Acrylamide, bis-acrylamide, and solutions containing these chemicals are toxic. Work with these solutions in a fume hood and while wearing gloves and eye protection.
AF0075 Mouse Cardiac Perfusion and Brain Collection
Embed brain in 4.5% Oxidized Agarose solution
Removing Mis-Aligned Tissue from an Agarose Block
Methodology/ Procedures: Mount Brain on Slide
Dispose of excess and used items appropriately

steps.title: Prepare 4.0% Oxidized Agarose Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the oxidized agarose solution based on the required final volume (100 ml, 250 ml, or 500 ml) using the specified quantities of Agarose, Sodium Periodate, and 50 mM Phosphate Buffer.

substeps.instruction: Combine Agarose, Sodium Periodate, and 50 mM Phosphate Buffer (initial suspension) in a flask at least 2.5 times the volume of the solution to avoid spilling.
Stir for 2-3 hours at room temperature with light protection.
Filter the solution using a 0.2 µm bottle top filter and a vacuum pump into a waste bottle.
Wash the filter 3 times with the specified volume of 50 mM Phosphate Buffer (wash buffer), pulling the liquid through between each application.

Resuspend the solution in the filter by adding half of the 'final suspension' volume of Phosphate Buffer, pour into a bottle, rinse the filter with the remaining 'final suspension' buffer, and transfer to the bottle.
Stir with a stir bar on a stir plate until homogeneous.
Aliquot into light-protected glass containers (~12.5 ml/brain).

steps.title: Prepare Embedding Mold
steps.instruction: Prepare the Peel-A-Way disposable embedding mold (22x22x20 mm) for specimen alignment.

substeps.instruction: Use a straight edge ruler to mark two adjacent sides of the mold with two straight, vertical lines, or attach printed grid lines using adhesive backing.
Label the mold with the specimen and block number.

steps.title: Heat Agarose Solution
steps.instruction: Heat the required amount of agarose (~12.5 ml/brain) in a glass beaker.

substeps.instruction: Stir or shake the solution before measuring to ensure proper concentration.
Heat in a microwave at 10-second intervals on low power (3-4), swirling intermittently to prevent overheating or bumping, until the solution is clear and watery.
Use a glass laboratory thermometer to monitor temperature.
Stop heating once the solution reaches 75ºC and allow it to cool on the bench to 60ºC before use.

steps.title: Embed Brain in Agarose
steps.instruction: Embed the perfusion-fixed adult mouse brain (stored in PBS with 0.1% Sodium Azide) into the agarose mold.

substeps.instruction: Cut approximately 2 cm off the tip of a 3 ml transfer pipette.
Remove the brain from the conical tube and dry it on a Kimwipe; ensure the surface is not wet for proper agarose adhesion.
Place the embedding mold on the metal plate.
Fill the mold to the top edge with 60ºC agarose using the modified pipette, avoiding air bubbles; top off with 3-4 drops over the edge.
Using fine tip dissecting forceps, submerge the brain to the bottom of the mold with the anterior-posterior axis vertical and the posterior end at the bottom.
Align the brain's mid-line with the grid lines on the metal plate and the mold's side markings.
Hold the brain upright with forceps until the agarose solidifies enough to support it.
Allow to solidify at room temperature for 20 minutes, then place in a labeled jar at 4°C for an additional 20 minutes to harden.

steps.title: Perform Acrylamide Coembedding
steps.instruction: Coembed the agarose-embedded tissue in an acrylamide solution to prepare for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a solution of 4.5% Surecast (Acrylamide:Bis-acrylamide ratio 29:1) and 0.5% VA-044 activator in PBS (per brain: 22ml PBS mixed with 0.13g activator, then add 3ml Surecast). Keep all components cold.
Soak the agarose-embedded tissue overnight at 4°C in this solution (>20mL volume).
Remove from the refrigerator and place on a shaker for 2 hours.
In a fume hood, prepare a mold with the brain ID and a small amount of acrylamide solution.
Transfer the tissue from the jar to the disposable mold using forceps, ensuring the agarose block is pushed all the way to the mold and the acrylamide fills the empty space.
Cover the mold securely with parafilm and bake in an oven at 40°C for a minimum of two hours to prevent oxygen inhibition of polymerization.

steps.title: Post-Bake Processing and Storage
steps.instruction: Remove the block from the mold and store it before mounting.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the block from the 40°C oven and remove it from the mold in a fume hood.
Place the mold on a clean surface and use a razor blade to remove excess agarose from the top and slice the four vertical edges.
Peel the embedding mold away from the block.
Place the block in an amber specimen container with ~25 ml of fresh Phosphate Buffer.
Cap, label, and store in a 4ºC fridge overnight (do not exceed 48 hours if in borohydride solution).

steps.title: Mount Block to Slide
steps.instruction: Attach the processed agarose block to a 1x3 glass slide for TissueCyte imaging.

substeps.instruction: Place the block on the slide with the olfactory bulb facing down and the brain aligned vertically (trim the base if necessary).
Apply a small amount of Loctite 404 adhesive to the roughened surface of the slide.
Position the block between two magnets with the right side of the brain facing the barcode and the olfactory bulb at the bottom.
Enter specimen information into the Laboratory Information Management System.
